name: Shelf Ghost Tank
description:
Not a manufactured item — a category. On the Shelf, a Ghost Tank is any sleeveless top that's been stripped, cut, bleached, painted, and re-stitched until its original identity is gone. The one in your hand might have started as a Meridian Transit Authority uniform, a Tokusen Industries promo shirt, or a kids' athletic set. Now it's been cut at the shoulders, the neckline widened with a blade, and stenciled with a crow skull or a glitch-art pattern in white house pigment. The hem is raw or knotted. Maybe a strip of reflective salvage tape runs diagonal across the back.

They sell in clusters at Shelf market stalls — three for Φ12, or individually from someone who takes their customization seriously enough to charge Φ18 for a specific piece. No two are identical. Wearing one is a statement that you came from somewhere specific and didn't bother to hide it.
what_it_says: You are from the Shelf, or you want that read, or you are an artist who works in the vernacular of scarcity. The authenticity is either real or very well studied.
manufacturer: Various — Shelf market vendors and individual makers
story_hooks: A Ghost Tank stencil pattern is being reproduced exactly by a Tier 4 fashion label — the original artist, a Shelf kid named Osei, has no legal recourse but a lot of friends.
A specific ghost tank was worn by someone during a riot six months ago; surveillance footage is grainy but the diagonal reflective stripe is distinctive.
A collector in Tier 4 pays absurd prices for authentic Ghost Tanks — their obsession with Shelf aesthetics has become something darker than appreciation.

physical_description.visual_profile: Deliberately deconstructed sleeveless top with radical shoulder cuts and widened neckline, creating an asymmetrical, aggressive silhouette. Raw edges and hand-applied artwork give it a street-modified aesthetic. Worn as a badge of sub-grade identity and personal history.
physical_description.fit: Loose and relaxed through the torso, with dramatic arm openings that extend nearly to the ribs. Neckline sits wide and loose, sometimes off-shoulder depending on cut severity. Emphasizes exposed skin and augmentation visibility.
physical_description.primary_material: Recycled cotton-synthetic blend or salvaged pre-consumer textile, stripped of original finish and re-treated with bleach, pigment, and occasional fabric glue reinforcement
physical_description.texture: Rough and tactile — raw hems that fray or are deliberately knotted, bleached areas with a papery quality, painted/stenciled sections with slightly raised pigment texture, salvage tape elements that are smooth and reflective by contrast
physical_description.color_scheme: Heavily bleached or faded base (cream, pale gray, off-white), overpainted with stark graphics in white house pigment, black stencil work, or occasional acid-bright accent colors. Reflective tape stripes in silver or neon accents.
physical_description.closures: None — completely open sleeveless design, sometimes with visible repair stitching or knots at raw edges
distinctive_features: Shoulder seams cut away or deliberately slashed open
Neckline widened with blade or shears, creating uneven raw edge
Hand-stenciled or painted graphics — crow skulls, glitch patterns, abstract designs
Raw or deliberately knotted hem edges
Salvaged reflective tape applied diagonally or as accent strips
Visible evidence of multiple alterations and re-stitching
Possible faint ghost image of original manufacturer branding or uniform marking beneath bleach
No care taken to hide seams or repair work — imperfection is intentional
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 — sub-grade and ungoverned. Signals rejection of corpo/commercial fashion and adoption of street modification culture.
physical_description.cultural_context: Shelf dweller, salvage-culture participant, or someone actively rejecting their previous social position. Wearing one announces: 'I have a past, I made this myself, and I'm not hiding where I came from.' Associated with Shelf markets, independent makers, and counter-corpo street culture.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately worn, distressed, and weathered. Fading, staining, and asymmetrical wear are features, not flaws. Might show patina from repeated wearing and exposure.
